Personality: Iuvantios, a prominent figure of the Patavini, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Iuvantios owes allegiance to the Mediterranean League, hailing from the noble house of Patavini. Historical Record: Son of Voltiomnos and Ostiala, of the Patavini, an Italic house of the Veneti. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
